# Design: Fix the edge cases found while specifying the core commands

## Context

Four independent defects across three crates (see the proposal). What the
code does today:

- **Main spec discovery** — `codev_engine::specs::list`
  (`crates/codev-engine/src/specs.rs:12-28`) walks `_codev/specs/` and keeps
  every file for which `relative.strip_suffix("spec.md")` succeeds. The
  match is on characters, not on the last path component: `draft-spec.md`
  yields the capability `draft-`. `validate::validate_spec` then reads
  `specs/draft-/spec.md`, gets `EngineError::Unreadable`, and the `?` in
  `validate_all` (`crates/codev-engine/src/validate/mod.rs:136-138`) aborts
  the whole report. The same list feeds `codev list --specs`, validate item
  resolution and `codev doctor` (`crates/codev-cli/src/commands.rs:631, 690,
  707, 752, 1644, 1661`). Sync and archive find deltas differently and are
  not affected. A plain `README.md` is already ignored (test
  `ignores_what_is_not_a_spec`).
- **Schema name vs folder** — `codev_engine::schemas::resolve`
  (`crates/codev-engine/src/schemas.rs:66-95`) finds a project schema by its
  folder and never compares the YAML `name`. `new_change`
  (`crates/codev-cli/src/commands.rs:499`) records `resolved.name()` — the
  YAML name — in `change.yaml`, while its JSON reports the requested
  (folder) name. Every later `change::load` resolves the recorded name and
  fails with `schema_not_found`.
- **Change named `archive`** — `ChangeId::parse`
  (`crates/codev-core/src/id.rs:18-27`) only checks kebab-case. The archive
  folder name is a constant of `Layout` (`crates/codev-core/src/layout.rs:22`)
  and a literal in `change::list` (`crates/codev-engine/src/change.rs:98`).
  `resolve_change` (`commands.rs:1712-1713`) goes through `ChangeId::parse`,
  so `--change archive` reaches `change::load`, which succeeds because the
  folder exists.
- **JSON paths** — `contract::v1` already has `to_slash`
  (`crates/codev-cli/src/contract.rs:812-813`), used by `validate`, `sync`,
  `archive`, the decision refs of `instructions`, sources and integration
  steps. The other documents build their path strings with
  `.display().to_string()`: in `contract.rs` (`resolvedOutputPath`:559,
  `dependencies[].path`:570, self-update `path`:158, doctor `root`:702,
  changelog `root` and paths:942, 972) and in `main.rs` (new change, `list`,
  `status`, sources, decision commands, init: 675-676, 706, 722, 740-741,
  934-1138, 1187-1188, 1202-1203, 1271). `commands.rs:1739-1741` holds a
  second copy of the conversion, `portable()`, for `config.yaml`.

Constraints: decision 0001 (functional core, imperative shell) and 0002
(the crate graph is the dependency rule) place each fix: name rules in
`codev-core`, disk-shaped discovery in `codev-engine` behind the
`FileSystem` port, serialization in `codev-cli::contract::v1`, which never
derives from the domain model (project context).

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals**

- Each defect is fixed at the single place every caller goes through, so
  that no command keeps the old behavior.
- No field of JSON contract v1 is added, renamed or removed; no new error
  code.

**Non-Goals**

- Turning an unreadable main spec into a finding instead of an execution
  error. Once discovery is exact, `Unreadable` only means a real I/O
  failure on a real `spec.md`, which is an execution error by design.
- Reserving names other than `archive`: it is the only folder `Layout`
  gives a meaning to under `_codev/changes/`.
- Normalizing paths written to files (`config.yaml` already uses `/`;
  `change.yaml` holds no path) or printed in human output.
- Repairing existing `change.yaml` files that recorded a mismatched schema
  name (see Migration Plan).

## Decisions

### Decision: A capability is a folder holding a file whose last component is `spec.md`

`specs::list` keeps a walked file only when its relative path is exactly
`spec.md` preceded by `/` (or is `spec.md` at the root, which still names no
capability); the capability is what precedes that `/`. Since every consumer
— `list --specs`, `validate`, item resolution, `doctor` — goes through this
function, one fix covers them all, and the validate requirement follows
without touching `validate_all`. Comparing path components with `Path`
would also work, but the walked paths are `/`-separated strings already
(the in-memory and real file systems both return them that way), so a
string check on `"/spec.md"` stays consistent with the existing code.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Making `validate_all` skip items it cannot read: hides real I/O failures
  and leaves `list --specs` and `doctor` listing phantom capabilities.

### Decision: A project schema whose `name` differs from its folder is `schema_invalid`

`schemas::resolve` is the only place that knows both the folder and the
parsed graph. After `ArtifactGraph::from_yaml`, for a project schema, it
compares `graph.schema().name` with the requested folder name and returns a
new `EngineError::SchemaNameMismatch { folder, declared }` mapped to the
existing code `schema_invalid`, with a message naming both and the fix
("rename the folder or set `name: <folder>`"). Because `list_schemas` and
`new_change` already go through `resolve`, `codev schemas` reports it as
`schema_unusable` and `new change` fails before writing, with no change to
either. The check is in the engine, not in `codev-core`'s schema parser,
because the parser receives only the YAML text and must stay ignorant of
where it came from (decision 0001). The built-in schema is unaffected: it
has no folder, and its embedded name is `spec-driven`.

As a consequence, `resolved.name()` and the requested name are always equal
for a project schema, so `new_change` records and reports the same name.
`new_change` is still changed to record the requested name explicitly, so
that the JSON `schemaName` and `change.yaml` cannot diverge again.

**Alternatives considered**:

- **The folder wins, `name` is ignored**: the schema would become usable
  as-is (the literal reading of "unusable"), but `name` would become a field
  that silently means nothing and the guide's instruction to match the
  folder would stay unenforced. Refusing costs one line of YAML, named in
  the message.
- **A new code `schema_name_mismatch`**: more precise, but every installed
  skill already handles `schema_invalid` and `schema_unusable`; the message
  carries the detail.

### Decision: `archive` is rejected by `ChangeId::parse`

`ChangeId::parse` refuses `archive` with `CoreError::InvalidChangeId` and
the reason "is reserved for archived changes", after the kebab-case rules so
that the first broken rule is still reported first. Every entry point —
`codev new change`, `resolve_change` for `--change`, the sync and archive
commands — already parses through it, so they all refuse with
`invalid_change_id`, and `codev new change archive` no longer reaches the
`change_exists` check. The reserved name is taken from the `Layout`
constant (`ARCHIVE_DIR`, made visible to `id.rs` inside `codev-core`), and
`change::list` uses that constant instead of its literal, so the folder
name lives in one place.

`is_valid` (`id.rs:48`) keeps checking kebab-case only: it is a format
predicate, and `change::list` already filters the archive folder before
calling it.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Checking in `new_change` only: `--change archive` would still compute a
  status over the archive folder, and `codev archive --change archive`
  would try to move the folder into itself.
- A new code `reserved_change_id`: rejected for the same reason as above —
  existing consumers already handle `invalid_change_id`.

### Decision: Every path of `contract::v1` goes through one conversion helper

`to_slash` becomes the single function, in `contract.rs`, that turns a
`Path` into a JSON string. Every `.display().to_string()` that feeds a v1
document — in `contract.rs` and in `main.rs` — is replaced by it; the
helper is made `pub(crate)` so `main.rs` and `commands.rs` reuse it, and
`portable()` in `commands.rs` delegates to it rather than duplicating the
replacement. The conversion stays `to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/")`:
it is a no-op on Unix and, as the existing comment explains, avoids the
doubled leading separator a component-wise join produces. A test in
`contract.rs` serializes each v1 document built from a Windows-style path
(constructed as a string, so it runs on every OS) and asserts that no `\`
remains.

**Alternatives considered**:

- A `serde` `serialize_with` on `PathBuf` fields: the v1 structs hold
  `String`s, by design (the contract never derives from the domain model);
  converting at construction keeps them that way.
- Converting in the engine: paths there are domain values used for I/O;
  the separator is a concern of the output contract only.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [A project relies on a schema whose `name` differs from its folder] →
  It was already unusable after creation; the new message names the exact
  fix. Called out in the release note.
- [A JSON consumer on Windows splits paths on `\`] → The documentation has
  always promised `/`, and Windows APIs accept `/`. Called out in the
  release note.
- [Self-update reports the executable path from `canonicalize`, which is a
  verbatim `\\?\C:\…` path on Windows] → It becomes `//?/C:/…`: only `/`
  separators, as required, but still a verbatim path. Stripping the prefix
  is left out of this change; the field is informational.
- [A missed `.display()` call keeps a backslash] → The contract test covers
  every v1 document; a `grep` for `display().to_string()` in
  `contract.rs` and `main.rs` is part of the review.
- [A capability folder literally named with a trailing `-spec` suffix] →
  Unaffected: `user-spec/spec.md` still yields `user-spec`, since only the
  last component is compared.

## Migration Plan

- No data migration is run. A change whose `change.yaml` recorded a
  mismatched schema name already failed with `schema_not_found`; its owner
  sets `schema:` to the folder name and fixes the schema's `name`, as the
  new `schema_invalid` message says.
- A folder `_codev/changes/archive/change.yaml`, created by the old
  behavior, is no longer reachable by name; it is removed by hand. No
  automatic cleanup, since it sits inside the archive.
- Rollback is a plain revert: no format or stored state changes.

# Proposal: Fix the edge cases found while specifying the core commands

## Why

While specifying the core commands (`2026-10-12-specify-core-commands`),
four behaviors that looked like bugs were left out of the specs and set
aside for their own change. Each one either breaks a command for the whole
project or leaves a change that no later command can use. With the specs
now covering the core commands, these are the remaining gaps between what
the tool does and what a user can reasonably expect.

## What Changes

- **Stray file in the specs folder.** A markdown file in `_codev/specs/`
  whose name only *ends* with `spec.md` (for example `draft-spec.md` or
  `user-auth/old-spec.md`) is mistaken for a capability. `codev validate`
  then aborts on the phantom capability, and `codev list --specs` lists it.
  A capability becomes strictly a folder holding a file named exactly
  `spec.md`; any other file is ignored by `list --specs` and by `validate`.
- **Schema whose `name:` does not match its folder.** Today
  `codev new change --schema my-flow` with `_codev/schemas/my-flow/schema.yaml`
  declaring `name: other` creates the change but records `schema: other`, so
  every later command on that change fails with `schema_not_found`. A
  project schema whose `name` differs from its folder becomes invalid
  (`schema_invalid`, naming both), so it is reported as `schema_unusable` by
  `codev schemas` and refused by `codev new change` before anything is
  written.
- **A change named `archive`.** `archive` is the archive folder of
  `_codev/changes/`, yet it passes the change name rules: the user gets a
  misleading `change_exists`, or, when the folder is missing, a change no
  one can list or archive. `archive` becomes a reserved change name, refused
  with `invalid_change_id` and a message saying it is reserved, by
  `codev new change` and by every command taking `--change`.
- **Backslashes in JSON paths on Windows.** Several JSON documents write
  paths with the platform separator (`changeRoot`, `planningHome`,
  `resolvedOutputPath`, `created`, `root`…), whereas the documentation
  already promises `/` on every OS. Every path in every JSON document is
  written with `/` separators.
- Documentation (English and French) is updated where it states these
  rules: change names, schema files, JSON paths.

**Assumptions** (this run had no one to ask):

- The stray file of the report is one whose name ends with `spec.md`: a
  plain `README.md` or `notes.md` is already ignored today, so it cannot be
  the file that broke validation.
- For a schema whose name differs from its folder, the fix refuses the
  schema with a clear reason rather than silently trusting the folder name:
  the `name` field then means something, and the one-line fix is named in
  the message. The alternative (folder name wins, `name` ignored) is
  discussed in the design.
- `archive` is refused with the existing `invalid_change_id` code rather
  than a new code, so the installed skills already handle it.
- The JSON path fix covers every command, not only the core ones, because
  the documented contract is global.
- Domains are ticked by judgement alone: the change holds only planning
  files, so there is no diff to go by yet.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `json-output` — the rules shared by every `--json` document, starting
  with the format of the paths it carries.

### Modified Capabilities

- `changes` — `archive` is a reserved change name; `codev list --specs`
  only counts files named exactly `spec.md`.
- `schemas` — a project schema's `name` must match its folder.
- `validation` — validation covers exactly the capabilities that have a
  main spec, and a stray file does not abort it.

### Removed Capabilities

None.

## Impact

- `codev-core`: the change name rule (reserved `archive`).
- `codev-engine`: discovery of the main specs, resolution of project
  schemas.
- `codev-cli`: the JSON documents of `new change`, `status`, `list`,
  `instructions`, `init`, `doctor`, `changelog`, `self-update` and the
  decision and sources commands, which must convert their paths the same
  way `validate`, `sync` and `archive` already do.
- JSON contract v1: no field is added, renamed or removed; on Windows, path
  values change from `\` to `/`, as documented.
- Documentation, both `docs/en` and `docs/fr`: `reference/cli.md` (change
  names), `reference/json-output.md` (paths), `guides/custom-schemas.md`
  (`name` matches the folder).

## Domains

- [ ] security
- [ ] personal-data
- [ ] user-interface
- [ ] performance
- [ ] operations
- [x] migration — a mismatched project schema is now refused, and JSON consumers on Windows receive `/` instead of `\`

## Release note

- Fixed: `codev validate` and `codev list --specs` no longer mistake a file
  whose name ends with `spec.md` (such as `draft-spec.md`) for a
  capability.
- Fixed: a project schema whose `name:` differs from its folder is now
  reported as unusable by `codev schemas` and refused by
  `codev new change`, instead of creating a change that no command can
  open. Rename the schema or its folder so that they match.
- Fixed: `archive` is now refused as a change name, since it is the folder
  of archived changes.
- Fixed: on Windows, every path in the JSON output now uses `/` separators,
  as the documentation states.

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: A change name is kebab-case and unique

A change name MUST consist of lowercase ASCII letters, digits and hyphens,
MUST NOT start or end with a hyphen, and MUST NOT contain two consecutive
hyphens; it MAY start with a digit. A change name MUST NOT be `archive`,
which names the folder of archived changes. `codev new change` SHALL refuse
any other name with the error code `invalid_change_id` and a message naming
the first rule broken (empty, leading or trailing hyphen, consecutive
hyphens, space, underscore, uppercase letter, the offending character, or a
reserved name). It SHALL refuse a name whose folder already exists with the
error code `change_exists`. A refused command writes nothing and exits with
code 1.

The commands taking `--change` SHALL apply the same rules to the name they
receive: `--change archive` fails with `invalid_change_id`, never acting on
the archive folder.

#### Scenario: Names accepted

- **WHEN** the user creates the changes `add-auth`, `100-add-feature` and
  `v2-migration`
- **THEN** each one is created

#### Scenario: Names that only contain the reserved word are accepted

- **WHEN** the user creates the changes `archive-old-specs` and
  `fix-archive`
- **THEN** each one is created

#### Scenario: An invalid name is refused with the rule it breaks

- **WHEN** the user runs `codev new change "Add Auth"`
- **THEN** the command fails with `invalid_change_id` and a message saying
  the name contains a space
- **AND** `_codev/changes/` is unchanged

#### Scenario: The reserved name `archive` is refused

- **GIVEN** an initialized project, whose `_codev/changes/archive/` exists
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev new change archive`
- **THEN** the command fails with `invalid_change_id`, not `change_exists`
- **AND** the message says that `archive` is reserved for archived changes
- **AND** `_codev/changes/archive/` is unchanged

#### Scenario: `archive` is refused even when the archive folder is missing

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/changes/archive/` does not exist
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev new change archive`
- **THEN** the command fails with `invalid_change_id`
- **AND** `_codev/changes/archive/change.yaml` does not exist

#### Scenario: `--change archive` is refused

- **GIVEN** an initialized project with archived changes
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status --change archive --json`
- **THEN** the command fails with `invalid_change_id` in `status`
- **AND** no artifact state is reported

#### Scenario: An existing name is refused

- **GIVEN** an active change `add-auth`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev new change add-auth`
- **THEN** the command fails with `change_exists`
- **AND** the existing `change.yaml` is unchanged

### Requirement: `codev list` lists the active changes and, with `--specs`, the capabilities

`codev list` SHALL list the active changes — the folders of
`_codev/changes/` other than `archive` whose name is a valid change name —
in alphabetical order. A folder whose name is not a valid change name is
ignored without error. When there is none, the human output SHALL say so
and name `codev new change <name>`. With `--json`, the document SHALL be
`{ "changes": [...], "root": <project root>, "status": [] }`.

`codev list --specs` SHALL list the capabilities that have a main spec: the
path, relative to `_codev/specs/`, of each folder holding a file named
exactly `spec.md`, nested folders included, in alphabetical order. A
`spec.md` placed directly in `_codev/specs/` names no capability. Any other
file — including one whose name merely ends with `spec.md`, such as
`draft-spec.md` — names no capability and is ignored without error. When
there is none, the human output SHALL say that specs appear when a change
is synced or archived. With `--json`, the document SHALL be
`{ "specs": [...], "root": <project root>, "status": [] }`.

#### Scenario: Active changes, archive excluded

- **GIVEN** the changes `fix-bug` and `add-auth`, an archived change, and a
  folder `Notes_2026` under `_codev/changes/`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev list --json`
- **THEN** `changes` is `["add-auth", "fix-bug"]`

#### Scenario: No active change

- **GIVEN** a project without active change
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev list`
- **THEN** the output names `codev new change`
- **AND** the exit code is 0

#### Scenario: Capabilities, nested ones included

- **GIVEN** main specs `_codev/specs/user-auth/spec.md` and
  `_codev/specs/identity/sso/spec.md`, and a file
  `_codev/specs/user-auth/README.md`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev list --specs --json`
- **THEN** `specs` is `["identity/sso", "user-auth"]`

#### Scenario: A file whose name ends with `spec.md` is not a capability

- **GIVEN** a main spec `_codev/specs/user-auth/spec.md`, and the files
  `_codev/specs/draft-spec.md` and `_codev/specs/user-auth/old-spec.md`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev list --specs --json`
- **THEN** `specs` is `["user-auth"]`
- **AND** `status` is empty

#### Scenario: No capability yet

- **GIVEN** a project without main spec
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev list --specs`
- **THEN** the output says that specs appear when a change is synced or
  archived

## Purpose

State the rules every `--json` document of codev follows, whatever the
command, so that a skill or a script parses the output the same way on
every operating system.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Paths in JSON documents use `/` separators on every OS

Every path value of a JSON document written by a codev command with
`--json` — absolute or relative, in any field or array, including
`root`, `planningHome`, `changeRoot`, `resolvedOutputPath`, `created`,
`path`, the dependencies' paths and the paths of findings — SHALL use `/` as
its only separator, on every operating system, Windows included. A path
SHALL NOT contain a doubled separator introduced by this conversion. On a
system whose separator is already `/`, the values are unchanged.

#### Scenario: Status of a change on Windows

- **GIVEN** a project at `C:\work\app` with a change `add-auth`, on Windows
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** `planningHome` is `C:/work/app`
- **AND** `changeRoot` is `C:/work/app/_codev/changes/add-auth`
- **AND** no path value contains `\`

#### Scenario: Instructions on Windows

- **GIVEN** a project at `C:\work\app` with a change `add-auth` whose
  proposal is written, on Windows
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions specs --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** `resolvedOutputPath` is
  `C:/work/app/_codev/changes/add-auth/specs/**/*.md`
- **AND** the path of the `proposal` dependency is
  `C:/work/app/_codev/changes/add-auth/proposal.md`

#### Scenario: A created change on Windows

- **GIVEN** a project at `C:\work\app`, on Windows
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev new change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** `changeRoot` is `C:/work/app/_codev/changes/add-auth`
- **AND** `created` lists `C:/work/app/_codev/changes/add-auth/change.yaml`

#### Scenario: Unchanged on a Unix system

- **GIVEN** a project at `/work/app` with a change `add-auth`, on Linux or
  macOS
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** `changeRoot` is `/work/app/_codev/changes/add-auth`

#### Scenario: A failed command keeps portable paths

- **GIVEN** a project at `C:\work\app` with no active change, on Windows
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status --json`
- **THEN** the document carries `no_active_change` in `status`
- **AND** every path value it still carries uses `/` separators

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: A schema file is validated before use

A `schema.yaml` SHALL be refused with `schema_unreadable` when it is not
valid YAML or holds a key codev does not know, and with `schema_invalid`,
naming the schema and the reason, when:

- `name` is empty or not kebab-case;
- for a project schema, `name` differs from the name of its folder
  `_codev/schemas/<folder>/` — the message names both and says to make them
  match;
- `artifacts` is empty;
- an artifact id is not kebab-case or is declared twice;
- an artifact has an empty `generates`;
- an artifact requires an artifact that does not exist, or itself;
- the dependencies form a cycle — the message names the artifacts
  involved;
- `apply.requires` is empty or names an artifact that does not exist;
- `apply.tracks` is empty.

`version` defaults to `1`. A command that needs a refused schema fails with
its code; `codev schemas` reports it as `schema_unusable`. Because a
refused schema fails before anything is written, `codev new change` never
records in `change.yaml` a schema name that no folder resolves.

#### Scenario: A minimal valid schema

- **GIVEN** a schema with a name, two artifacts, `apply.requires` and
  `apply.tracks`, and no `version`
- **WHEN** it is read
- **THEN** it is accepted with version `1`

#### Scenario: An unknown key

- **GIVEN** a schema holding the key `artefacts`
- **WHEN** it is read
- **THEN** it is refused with `schema_unreadable`

#### Scenario: Structural defects

- **WHEN** a schema requires a missing artifact, declares an artifact twice,
  declares no artifact, has an empty `apply.requires`, or has a cycle
  between `a` and `b`
- **THEN** each is refused with `schema_invalid`
- **AND** the cycle message names `a` and `b`

#### Scenario: A project schema named like its folder is accepted

- **GIVEN** a valid `_codev/schemas/lite/schema.yaml` declaring `name: lite`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev new change quick --schema lite`
- **THEN** its `change.yaml` holds `schema: lite`
- **AND** `codev status --change quick` lists the artifacts of `lite`

#### Scenario: A project schema named unlike its folder is listed as unusable

- **GIVEN** an otherwise valid `_codev/schemas/my-flow/schema.yaml`
  declaring `name: other`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev schemas --json`
- **THEN** the exit code is 0
- **AND** `schemas` does not list `my-flow` nor `other`
- **AND** `status` holds a warning `schema_unusable` whose message names
  `my-flow` and `other`

#### Scenario: A project schema named unlike its folder creates no change

- **GIVEN** an otherwise valid `_codev/schemas/my-flow/schema.yaml`
  declaring `name: other`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev new change quick --schema my-flow`
- **THEN** the command fails with `schema_invalid`, whose message names
  `my-flow` and `other`
- **AND** `_codev/changes/quick/` does not exist

#### Scenario: A mismatched project `spec-driven` does not fall back silently

- **GIVEN** a `_codev/schemas/spec-driven/schema.yaml` declaring
  `name: my-driven`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev new change quick`
- **THEN** the command fails with `schema_invalid`
- **AND** the built-in `spec-driven` is not used in its place

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Validation covers exactly the capabilities with a main spec

When it validates the main specs (`codev validate --all`, `--specs`, or a
named capability), the validator SHALL cover exactly the capabilities that
`codev list --specs` lists: the folders of `_codev/specs/` holding a file
named exactly `spec.md`. Any other file under `_codev/specs/` — a
`README.md`, notes, or a file whose name merely ends with `spec.md` — SHALL
be ignored: it produces no item, no finding and no execution error, and it
MUST NOT stop the other items from being validated.

#### Scenario: A stray file whose name ends with `spec.md`

- **GIVEN** a well-formed main spec `_codev/specs/user-auth/spec.md` and a
  file `_codev/specs/draft-spec.md`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate --specs --json`
- **THEN** the items are exactly `user-auth`
- **AND** the root `status` is empty
- **AND** the process exits with code `0`

#### Scenario: A stray markdown file next to the capabilities

- **GIVEN** a well-formed main spec `_codev/specs/user-auth/spec.md`, a file
  `_codev/specs/README.md` and a file `_codev/specs/user-auth/old-spec.md`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate --all`
- **THEN** the report covers `user-auth` and the active changes only
- **AND** the process exits with code `0`

#### Scenario: A stray file is not a validatable item

- **GIVEN** a file `_codev/specs/draft-spec.md` and no folder `draft-`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate draft- --json`
- **THEN** the root `status` carries an error entry with the code
  `unknown_item`
